imaios_cmp.says: a cutaneous fold forming a small pouch on the antitragic border in the carnivore; only its rostral wall is supported by cartilage

wikipedia_hp.cite: Wikipedia, 'Henry's pocket' (cites August 2009 Consultations in Feline Internal Medicine 6:319-321; Cole 2010 Vet Dermatol; Neuber & Nuttall 2017)
wikipedia_hp.says: a fold of skin forming an open pouch on the lower posterior part of the external ear, at the approximate location of the human antitragus; particularly noticeable on the domestic cat; no size given

uberon_cmp.says: fold of skin at the caudal border of the auricle

lanz_wood_2005.cite: Lanz O.I., Wood B.C. (2004/2005) Surgery of the ear and pinna. Vet Clin North Am Small Anim Pract 34(2)
lanz_wood_2005.says: auricular cartilage is elastic and thin at the apex and then rolls into a semitube at the base; the pinna is covered with skin on both sides, closely attached to the perichondrium; the free edge of the auricular cartilage is called the helix; the antitragus is a thin cartilaginous plate caudal to the tragus; no thickness numbers

wikivet_pinna.says: skin on both sides, more tightly on the medial/concave side than the convex side; hair on the convex side like the body, on the concave side variable; medial and lateral crus of the helix at the opening of the external ear canal

kumar_2016.cite: Kumar & Roman-Auerhahn, Anatomy of the Canine and Feline Ear (Veterian Key 2016) - already in references/cat-hair-streams.md
kumar_2016.says: the external ear canal of the cat is devoid of hairs

mivart_1881.cite: Mivart 1881, The Cat, ch. II s.1 (via references/cat-hair-streams.md)
mivart_1881.says: the deep cavity of each ear is directed forwards and outwards; long hairs inside each ear and sometimes on its tip

no_thickness_found.says: Searched (text only): feline pinna thickness, auricular cartilage thickness, cat skin thickness by region (incl. Zanna et al. 2017 Can J Vet Res 81:292 - ultrasound, abstract ranks neck thickest / abdomen thinnest, no pinna value read). NO cited mm value for cat pinna, cartilage or pouch-flap thickness was found; every tissue thickness below is an ESTIMATE, flagged.

coat_depth_limits.why: the v1 skin inset retracted the ear tips ~2 mm: ear_back (0.9 typ) + ear_inner (1.5 typ) = 2.4 mm exceeds the envelope's thickness within ~1.5-2 mm of the apex; the pocket lip is the same failure mode (its envelope is only ~1 mm thick 0.5 mm below the free edge)
coat_depth_limits.rule: per wall: D = d_face1 + d_face2 (coat depths at the wall's two envelope faces); D_max(p) = max(0, T_env(p) - t_tissue(p)); scale = smin(1, D_max / D; k 0.05); each face depth *= scale. T_env(p) = local envelope wall thickness, two-sided ray from the face point along -normal to the opposite envelope face (exact raycast on a crop). t_tissue from anatomy (estimates above). Apply as a smooth field (C3b: no crease where the clamp starts; coat_check gradient limit X = 4 still holds).

tip.thickness_measure: 2 x area / perimeter of the exact Tripo section perpendicular to the ear axis (a thin-wall mean; local rim values are lower - use the local T_env in the build, this table for the probe)
tip.apex_requirement: skin apex within 0.5 mm of the envelope apex along the ear axis (precision budget; photo ear-edge fringe 0.68 mm incl. optics says the coat at the outline is thin anyway): the skin section 0.5 mm below the envelope apex must be non-empty, i.e. total depth there <= 1.33 (L) / 1.19 (R) mm, about 0.6 mm per face; ramp up to the regional values by ~4 mm below the tip
tip.geometry_note: side apex angle ~57-59 deg (REVIEW_ears S3): an uncapped inset of D total retracts a wedge apex by ~D / (2 sin 29 deg) ~ 1.0 x D - 2.4 mm reproduces the observed ~2 mm

flap.tissue_mm: 0.6 at the free edge (doubled skin, ESTIMATE), joining the ear wall at the floor
flap.slot_faces: depth 0 (furless) - the slot keeps Tripo's walls, so its depth and gaps transfer to the skin unchanged

max_outer_face_depth_mm.basis: p10 of the envelope lip (L, the thinner) minus 0.6 mm tissue, capped at coat.json ear_back max 1.5

flap.requirement: the free edge on the skin stays within 0.5 mm of the envelope's free edge, and the flap never thins below 0.5 mm

sdf_recipe.convention: f < 0 inside tissue; ear frame mm; min = union, max = intersection; NO smoothing operator may act inside the slot (its blend radius is forced to 0 within 0.5 mm of the Slot volume)
sdf_recipe.S1_skin_base: E_skin(p) = E_env(p) + d'(p): the envelope SDF inset by the CLAMPED coat depth (coat_depth_limits.rule); d' = 0 on furless zones incl. 'pocket_slot'
sdf_recipe.S2_slot_air: Slot(p): per section h (plane perpendicular to the axis) local coords a = depth below the free-edge level along -m(h) and b = signed offset across the slot from its midline c(h, a). Midline and half-gap from the tables (free edge, floor, gap at 50 / 90 % depth, narrowest gap), linearly interpolated in a and h. slot2D = |b - c(h,a)| - g(h,a)/2 for a < D(h) - r_f; distance to the floor disk of radius r_f = max(0.25, gap_min/2) beyond; open on the mouth side (a < 0 extends 3 mm outward along +m). Sweep over h in the slot range; below the lower end D(h) -> 0 over 0.5 mm; above the upper end no cap (the slot opens continuously into the conch's lateral bay - LOG_ears E22).
sdf_recipe.S3_carve: E_pk = max(E_skin, -Slot(p)) - a HARD max, so the slot is air by construction
sdf_recipe.S4_flap_shell: Flap(p) = max(|Sigma(p)| - t_flap(a)/2, Bound(p)). Sigma = signed distance to the flap MID-SHEET: in each section the curve parallel to the slot's lateral wall at t_flap(a)/2 lateral of it, from the free edge (a = 0) to the floor level (a = D) where it roots into the ear wall. t_flap(a) = clamp(T_lip_env(a) - d_outer'(a), 0.6, T_lip_env(a)). |Sigma| - t/2 makes the free edge a ROUNDED U-turn of radius t_flap(0)/2 ~ 0.3 mm: the outer skin turning back into the inner skin (the free edge's definition). Bound clips the sheet to a >= 0 and to the flap's h extent (L -6.0..slot top; R -6.0..slot top).
sdf_recipe.S5_assemble: E_ear = smin(max(E_pk, -FlapZone(p)), Flap(p); k_eff) where FlapZone = the tissue lateral of the slot midline within the pocket's h range (replaced by the explicit shell) and k_eff = 0.4 mm * clamp((Slot(p) - 0.5) / 0.5, 0, 1) - the blend joins the flap's root to the outer ear surface but cannot reach into the slot
sdf_recipe.S6_helix: Tube(p) = |p - rim_in(s)| - r_h(s), rim_in = the rim polyline moved r_h toward the concave (front) side and rotated about the rim tangent by the curl angle; margin = smin(plate, Tube; k 0.3) with the tube's outermost point kept ON the envelope outline (the photo sees the outline); r_h 0.5-0.9 mm, curl 90 deg at the base -> 0 at 10 mm below the tip
sdf_recipe.S7_conch: semitube at the base (inner radius from the base sections' front concavity, ~9.7 mm deep at h 5 per ears_sections - a SOUND near-base number +-0.6 mm under tilt) narrowing to a 4-6 mm canal opening on its floor, a blind tube >= 8 mm deep, hairless; not visible in the photo (clay check only)

P1_pocket_section.what: C6b's geometric probe: a section through the pocket shows TWO skin layers (the flap) and an OPEN slot of depth D +- tol
P1_pocket_section.how: for each ear and each h in the slot range at 0.25 mm: exact plane section of the BUILT skin perpendicular to the ear axis (paws_lib.plane_section on a crop of faces within 30 mm of the pocket centre), lateral chain (lateral > 0), deepest air-side hull notch (ears_lib.deepest_below_hull), free edge by the running-max rule (delta 0.3 mm). Then on the line across the slot at 50 % depth (perpendicular to the mouth direction, in the section plane) the crossing sequence from the conch side outward must read tissue -> AIR (slot) -> tissue (flap, both faces skin) -> AIR (outside the ear).

pass.two_layers: the crossing sequence above at >= 90 % of the slot heights and at every height within 2 mm of the deepest
pass.open: narrowest wall gap >= 0.25 mm at levels >= 10 % above the floor, and the slot midline at 50 % depth is outside the tissue (SDF > 0)
pass.depth: slot depth below the free edge = the table value +-0.5 mm per height (L h -5.5..-2.75 from pocket_sections_L, the rest Phase 1); max depth 12.2 +-0.5 (L) / 11.84 +-0.5 (R)
pass.extent: aspect > 2 run within one step (0.25 mm) of L -5.5..+1.5 / R -3.75..+3.75, or within the stated +-1 step
pass.flap: skin lip thickness 0.5 mm below the free edge in [0.5, 1.4] mm; free edge within 0.5 mm of the envelope's

planted_failures: a solid lump: the slot filled with tissue (crossing sequence fails, slot midline inside tissue)
a slot closed by fill: smooth union with k = 1.5 mm across the slot at 50 % depth (narrowest gap < 0.25)
the floor raised 1.0 mm (depth fails by > 0.5)
the flap fused to the conch wall over its top 2 mm (crossing sequence fails at those heights)
a zero-thickness flap sheet (lip < 0.5 mm; manifold check C2 fails)
Phase 1's L flap top used as the free edge (depth +2.8 mm at h -5.5..-2.75 - the B2 error)

open_decisions.for: orchestrator -> person (it touches the APPROVED C3 wording 'inner ear sits ON the envelope')
open_decisions.finding: Tripo's ear is a SOLID WEDGE, not a cupped plate: mean wall (2A/P of exact sections) 7.9 / 8.9 mm at 20 mm below the tip and 9.1 / 9.8 at 25 mm (L / R); the conch floor 14.6 / 15.6 mm thick at h 10 (LOG_ears E20). Cited anatomy: an elastic cartilage plate thin at the apex, rolling into a semitube at the base, with skin on both faces (lanz_wood_2005). The photo sees the outline, the rims and the pink inner surface's shading - not the cup's depth.

options.A_C3_literal: inner pink skin ON Tripo's front surface: the ear stays a solid ~8-15 mm wedge (a Tripo artefact kept as anatomy)
options.B_anatomy: thin cupped plate: back skin = envelope inset by ear_back; front skin = the back skin offset by the plate thickness (1.0-1.5 mm mid, ESTIMATE); rims and outline stay on the envelope; the cup deepens behind Tripo's front surface by up to ~6-7 mm at mid-height; the pocket recipe is unchanged (its slot walls stay on the envelope)

open_decisions.recommendation: B (anatomy; the photo cannot see the depth, so Tripo's depth is unsupported invention), pending the person's approval; the pocket and tip probes hold in either option

open_decisions.finding: the slot interior needs its own furless zone ('pocket_slot'); inner_ear_pink's gradient test misses the slot's lateral/medial-facing walls

this re-measure is a scratch tool (%TEMP%/p2prep_ears/flap_edge.py); record it in engine/log/TOOLMAKING.md (this brief could write only this file). REVIEW_ears B2's other fixes (split runs at floor/edge steps, a P5 plant at the lowest slot section) are folded into probe P1's planted failures.

tables.note: every 0.25 mm in h over the slot +-; source per row ('phase1_sound' = the free edge is the hull-bridge end and Phase 1's number is reproduced; 'remeasured_p2prep_free_edge' = REPLACES Phase 1's flap top). envelope_lip_thickness = distance from the flap's inner face at s mm below the free edge to its outer face, on the Tripo ENVELOPE (fur included on the outer face).

tool_record.reasoning: B2 says the L 'flap top' is the outer bulge; the free edge is where the flap's outer skin turns back into its inner skin, so walking floor -> mouth the level along the mouth direction must stop rising there. A running maximum with a fall-back tolerance (0.3 mm, ~0.6 x mesh edge; +-1 step 0.15 / 0.6) finds it without a smoothing scale; when no fall-back exists the hull-bridge end is the free edge, so the rule reduces to Phase 1 wherever Phase 1 was right (all of R, L above -2.5) - a built-in regression check.
checks_done: reproduces Phase 1 R slot numbers exactly (free edge = bridge end at every R slot height)
reproduces REVIEW_ears r7 L depths to 0.01 mm at h -5.5 / -4.25 / -4.0 / -3.0
L free-edge line continuous after the fix (max step 0.50 mm vs Phase 1's 6.7 mm jump)
limits: delta 0.3 misses the turn at L h -5.5 (it turns at 0.15): the lowest section is delta-sensitive
rows with depth < 1.5 mm (floor ripples at L h -5.75, -7.5, -7.75) dropped as below-slot
lip thickness = point-to-polyline distance, a wedge's local thickness, fur included
tool_record.memory_and_inputs: one tripo_welded.npz load + faces within 60 mm of each ear origin (130 k / 133 k faces), exact plane sections only; ~13 s per run; peak well under 1 GB; free memory checked >= 3 GB before each run
